【原视频简介】
This mini PC can already game surprisingly well, but I wanted to know how much more performance was hiding in it, and whether a full-size desktop CPU cooler could actually unlock more FPS.

So I took the Beelink SER9 Max, tested it stock, pushed the power limits and iGPU clocks, then strapped a massive desktop tower cooler to it and ran the same gaming benchmarks again.

I tested Shadow of the Tomb Raider, Cyberpunk, Hitman 3 and Cinebench R23 to compare stock performance, tuned performance, temperatures, power draw and the final tower-cooler setup.

The gaming gains were small, but the cooling difference was ridiculous. The tower setup massively reduced temperatures and gave the CPU much more thermal headroom, especially in Cinebench.

And because apparently that still wasn’t enough, I also tried running an external GPU over USB4.

That part went well.

Thanks to Beelink for sending the SER9 Max over for me to test. They did not pay for this video, had no involvement in the testing or results, and did not have any input into the video before upload.

Hardware:
Beelink SER9 Max
AMD Ryzen AI 7 H 350
Radeon 860M integrated graphics
32GB DDR5
1TB SSD

Benchmarks:
Shadow of the Tomb Raider
Cyberpunk
Hitman 3
Cinebench R23

If you like mini PC gaming, PC hardware mods, ridiculous cooling experiments, overclocking, iGPU tuning and generally making computers do things they were never designed to do, you’re in the right place.

Not a review.
Not sensible.
Just seeing how far it can go.
